## The defect

Bug `2c4b-3cd9-8bb0-4493` (velvet-prebeloved-discus) proved a defect class: a function whose
DEFAULT ARGUMENT is a name imported at module level freezes that binding at import time, so a
test that patches the symbol on its DEFINING module only reaches the consumer when the consumer
happens not to have been imported yet. Ticket `5ea3-76e5-480a-4464` already ruled this construct
a defect and established the remedy — a named call-time indirection (`_retry_sleep`, and
`acli_subprocess._backoff_sleep`) — documented in the `_retry_sleep` docstring at
`src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/access_check.py:44-58`.

A construct sweep run during `2c4b` found the 5ea3 remediation did NOT convert every site. These
are LATENT (no test trips them today because every current call site injects the dependency
explicitly), so they are filed rather than fixed inside a bug fix's authorisation:

* `src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/_ref_lock.py:558` — `steal(..., sleep_fn=time.sleep)`
* `src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/_advisory_lock.py:161` — `steal_pass_lock(..., sleep_fn=time.sleep)`
* `src/rebar/metrics/analyzers/_jscpd.py:18` — `run: Runner = subprocess.run`

Why they matter despite being latent: the suite contains GLOBAL `time.sleep` and
`subprocess.run` patches that these frozen defaults would silently escape — notably the
repo-isolation guard at `tests/unit/test_repo_isolation_guard.py:184`, whose `fail_sleep` exists
to fail loudly if anything sleeps. A real sleep reached through a frozen default slips past it.
The moment any caller stops injecting explicitly, each becomes the `2c4b` bug again.

Out of scope for `2c4b`: that bug fix is authorised to restore the invariant at the seam it
proved (`access_check.py`), not to refactor three unrelated modules.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Each of the three sites resolves its dependency at CALL time, mirroring the established
      `_retry_sleep` / `_backoff_sleep` indirection, with production behaviour byte-identical.
- [ ] An explicitly passed `sleep_fn=` / `run=` still wins over the seam.
- [ ] A test proves the seam is reachable: patch the symbol on its defining module AFTER the
      consumer module is resident in `sys.modules`, and observe the patch take effect.
- [ ] No new dependency, no behaviour widening, no weakened test.
